title: Al-'Adiyat 100:9-11 with words spaced, and the questions
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
unit: Summer 1: Al-'Adiyat, Az-Zalzalah and reading from the mushaf
source: Written for quran/y2 lesson 51 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Al-'Adiyat 100:9-11 with words spaced, and the questions)
intro: Lesson 51. Read each word slowly, pointing with your finger. Only the Arabic is the Qur'an; the English is a translation of its meaning.

arabic.text: ۞ أَفَلَا يَعْلَمُ إِذَا بُعْثِرَ مَا فِى ٱلْقُبُورِ (٩) وَحُصِّلَ مَا فِى ٱلصُّدُورِ (١٠) إِنَّ رَبَّهُم بِهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍۢ لَّخَبِيرٌۢ (١١)

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: But does he not know that when the contents of the graves are scattered
And that within the breasts is obtained,
Indeed, their Lord with them, that Day, is [fully] Acquainted.

keywords.def: the chests: what is in our hearts
fully aware: one of Allah's names

questions.q: Chunk and link Al-'Adiyat 100:9-11 with the teacher.
Listening turns: today's group says 100:9-11 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: say it softly 3 times looking, 3 times without.
questions.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.

questions.q: Tell a grown-up one good thing you will do only for Allah.
questions.a: For example: help at home without being asked.
A) fully aware of us. 100:11: 'their Lord with them, that Day, is [fully] Aware.'

questions.q: Al-'Adiyat 100:9: «أَفَلَا يَعْلَمُ ...» Which word comes next?
Think again: Allah knows what is in every heart. How does that make you feel?
questions.a: Safe and careful: Allah knows our good intentions, so we try to keep our hearts clean.
